note: Selectable presets for the v0.2 session demand model (SPEC 2.4). Every field here is a PLANNING ASSUMPTION, not a measurement. A preset fills the same inputs a user would type by hand: headcount, session rate, the workload mix, and the per-turn token shape for each workload type. Every number stays editable, and an edited value is labelled user_override rather than silently recomputed. No preset is evidence and none backs a modelled_p95_capacity verdict (SPEC 6.5). UNITS: every `fields` entry is written verbatim into the input of the same id by app.js:applyWorkloadPreset, so f-mix-* and f-peak-frac are PERCENTAGES here (70, not 0.7) and must stay in the units the screen shows. `defaults.peak_concurrency_fraction` below is the separate engine-side name and stays a FRACTION, because app.js:pctInput divides the on-screen percent by 100 before demand.js ever sees it.

provenance.basis: order-of-magnitude planning shapes, not customer telemetry

shape_note: Token shapes are per TURN. RAG carries retrieved context in the input; Graph RAG carries a larger multi-hop context; Agentic multiplies both by tool-call round trips, which is why its per-session total is roughly 8x RAG's. Those gaps are the reason the mix is modelled per workload instead of as one averaged shape.

presets.label: Support desk
presets.summary: Mostly short chat with some retrieval
presets.assumption_note: steady daytime traffic, short answers, a modest knowledge-base lookup on roughly a third of sessions

presets.label: Internal knowledge base
presets.assumption_note: employees querying policy and product documents; long retrieved context, short answers, heavy prompt-cache reuse across a shared corpus

presets.label: Graph RAG analytics
presets.summary: Multi-hop retrieval over a linked corpus
presets.assumption_note: analysts traversing entity relationships; each turn pulls several hops of context, so input dominates output by more than 10:1

presets.label: Agentic platform
presets.assumption_note: multi-step agents re-reading their own context on every tool round trip; the highest token intensity per session by roughly an order of magnitude, and the case where self-hosting is most likely to pay back

presets.label: Mixed enterprise
presets.summary: An even spread across all four workloads
presets.assumption_note: a platform team serving several teams at once; useful as a starting point when the mix is not yet known
